title: sequenceFiniteCoherence
statement:
Use the coefficient sequence module categories, chosen geometric and scalar comparisons, and bracketing interpretation of [def-trf-quotient-system-coherence-data]. For any scheme-indexed family of categories and contravariant functors U, let c be an invertible compositor and e an invertible identity comparison. Assume the explicitly transported three-arrow associativity equation and both unit equations. Then any two binary bracketings of the same finite path yield equal functors up to equality and equal comparisons after transport along that equality. Empty and singleton paths are included. The exact hypotheses and transport direction are those of the Lean signature below.

Lean statement:
theorem sequenceFiniteCoherence
    (D : Scheme.{t} → Type a) [∀ X, Category.{v} (D X)]
    (U : ∀ {X Y : Scheme.{t}}, (X ⟶ Y) → (D Y ⥤ D X))
    (c : ∀ {X Y Z : Scheme.{t}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z), U (f ≫ g) ≅ U g ⋙ U f)
    (e : ∀ X : Scheme.{t}, U (𝟙 X) ≅ 𝟭 (D X))
    (hA : ∀ {T X Y Z : Scheme.{t}} (f : Z ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ X) (h : X ⟶ T),
      (c (f ≫ g) h).hom ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft (U h) (c f g).hom =
        eqToHom (congrArg (fun f ↦ U f) (Category.assoc f g h)) ≫
          (c f (g ≫ h)).hom ≫ Functor.whiskerRight (c g h).hom (U f))
    (hL : ∀ {X Y : Scheme.{t}} (f : X ⟶ Y),
      (c (𝟙 X) f).hom ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft (U f) (e X).hom =
        eqToHom (congrArg (fun f ↦ U f) (Category.id_comp f)))
    (hR : ∀ {X Y : Scheme.{t}} (f : X ⟶ Y),
      (c f (𝟙 Y)).hom ≫ Functor.whiskerRight (e Y).hom (U f) =
        eqToHom (congrArg (fun f ↦ U f) (Category.comp_id f)))
    {X Y : Scheme.{t}} {p : Quiver.Path X Y} (a b : IntegralQuotientBracketing p) :
    ∃ h : integralQuotientBracketFunctor D U a = integralQuotientBracketFunctor D U b,
      integralQuotientBracketComparison D U c e a ≪≫ eqToIso h =
        integralQuotientBracketComparison D U c e b

proof.text: Define sequenceNormalFunctor by recursion on paths: the empty path is the identity functor and cons p f is U f followed by the normal functor of p. Define sequenceNormalMap from U(composePath p) recursively, using e for nil and c followed by left whiskering for cons. Induction on the second path identifies the normal functor of a concatenation with the composite of the two normal functors.

proof.text: Prove that equality transports commute with left whiskering, with the compositor, and with horizontal composition of natural transformations, each by equality induction. Prove sequenceNormalMap_comp by induction on the second path. The nil case is the right-unit equation hR and whiskering interchange. In the cons case, whisker the inductive equality, move its source transport through c, apply hA, and use whiskering interchange; equality transports compose by proof irrelevance.

proof.text: Induct on IntegralQuotientBracketing to identify its functor with the normal path functor and its comparison hom with sequenceNormalMap after transport. The nil case is reflexivity and the single case is hL. For comp, use the two inductive equalities, horizontal transport compatibility and sequenceNormalMap_comp, cancelling the normal-functor concatenation transport.
